classification.difficultyReason: Infer successive area halvings from diagonals and midpoints before comparing triangle areas.

content.prompt: In the diagram opposite, $ABCD$ is a square with diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ meeting at $X$, $Z$ is the midpoint of $BC$ and $Y$ is the midpoint of $XC$. Find the following ratios of areas.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 20, square diagram to the right
spec.description: Unshaded square with both diagonals and segments XZ and YZ. Ordinary source blue strokes become house black. Labels preserve their source sides.
spec.mathematics: A top left, B top right, C bottom right, D bottom left; X is the diagonal intersection; Z is the midpoint of BC; Y is the midpoint of XC.
spec.answerVisibility: All geometry and labels are permanent givens; no answers are shown.

answer.worked: The diagonals divide the square into four equal-area triangles. Hence $\operatorname{area}(\triangle AXD)=\operatorname{area}(\triangle AXB)$, so the ratio is $1:1$.

answer.short:
$2:1$

The midpoint $Z$ halves the area of triangle $XBC$.
answer.worked:
Triangles $ZXB$ and $ZXC$ have equal bases $BZ=ZC$ and the same perpendicular height from $X$ to $BC$. Each has half the area of triangle $XBC$. Triangle $AXD$ has the same area as triangle $XBC$.

$$\begin{align*}\operatorname{area}(\triangle AXD):\operatorname{area}(\triangle ZXB)&=1:\frac12\\\operatorname{area}(\triangle AXD):\operatorname{area}(\triangle ZXB)&=2:1\end{align*}$$

answer.short:
$4:1$

Two successive midpoint divisions halve the area twice.
answer.worked:
Since $Z$ is the midpoint of $BC$, triangle $ZXC$ has half the area of triangle $XBC$. Since $Y$ is the midpoint of $XC$, triangles $ZXY$ and $ZYC$ have equal bases and the same perpendicular height from $Z$ to $XC$. Thus triangle $ZYC$ has one-quarter the area of triangle $XBC$, which equals the area of triangle $AXD$.

$$\begin{align*}\operatorname{area}(\triangle AXD):\operatorname{area}(\triangle ZYC)&=1:\frac14\\\operatorname{area}(\triangle AXD):\operatorname{area}(\triangle ZYC)&=4:1\end{align*}$$

answer.short:
$8:1$

Triangle $DBC$ contains two quarter-square triangles; triangle $XYZ$ is one-quarter of a quarter-square triangle.
answer.worked:
Triangle $DBC$ consists of the equal-area triangles $DXC$ and $XBC$, so its area is twice that of triangle $XBC$. The midpoint $Z$ halves triangle $XBC$, and the midpoint $Y$ halves triangle $ZXC$. Thus triangle $XYZ$ has one-quarter the area of triangle $XBC$.

$$\begin{align*}\operatorname{area}(\triangle DBC):\operatorname{area}(\triangle XYZ)&=2:\frac14\\\operatorname{area}(\triangle DBC):\operatorname{area}(\triangle XYZ)&=8:1\end{align*}$$
